extracted.intended_audience: media activists, FAIR supporters, and members of the public who write letters/emails to journalists or want to contact news outlets
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and a compiled list of contact channels (addresses, phone numbers, email/forms, social handles) for television, radio, newspapers, magazines, and wire services to support media activism and sending letters to journalists. Also asks readers to send copies of their outreach to FAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send copies of your letters to FAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: FAIR wants to hear about your media activism. Please send copies of your letters to journalists to fair@fair.org or to: FAIR 124 West 30th Street, Suite 201 New York, NY 10001
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAIR notes: 'We can’t always respond, but we do look at everything.' This is the primary procedural request on the page—submit copies of your outreach by email or physical mail so FAIR can review and sometimes follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use program-specific email contacts/handles for TV programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists 'Email Contacts for ABC news programs' and specific handles for programs and anchors (e.g. @ABC, @abcpolitics, @ThisWeekABC, @GStephanopoulos, @ABCWorldNews, @DavidMuir).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contacting network TV shows, target the program-specific email/forms or the program/anchor social handles provided for higher relevance (examples given for ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox, NBC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use network 'email forms' for programs when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries state 'Email forms for all CBS news programs', 'Email forms for CNBC programs', and 'Email forms for all CNN news programs'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the network provides a centralized email form for program feedback, use that form to reach the applicable show(s) rather than generic addresses. The page repeatedly points users to those program-specific/email-form routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use show-specific email addresses for feedback/comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Some shows have direct emails: e.g., Fox News comments@foxnews.com; Special Report With Bret Baier: special@foxnews.com; Hannity: hannity@foxnews.com; Tucker Carlson Tonight: comments@foxnewsinsider.com; NBC News Today: today@nbc.com; Rachel Maddow Show: Rachel@msnbc.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target these direct show addresses for comments or feedback intended for a particular program or host for a more direct channel than general network addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use feedback/contact pages for networks and programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The page points to network feedback pages or contact pages (e.g., MSNBC 'Feedback page', NBC 'NBC News contact page', NPR 'Contact form').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a feedback or contact page is listed, follow that link/form to submit comments, tips, or complaints—these pages often route to the correct desk or producer faster than general mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use letters-to-the-editor addresses for newspapers and magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: For newspapers and magazines the page lists explicit 'Letters to the Editor' addresses and links (examples: Los Angeles Times 'Send a letter to the editor', New York Times letters@nytimes.com, The Atlantic letters: letters@theatlantic.com, Time 'Letters to the Editor: letters@time.com', Washington Post letters@washpost.com, WSJ wsj.ltrs@wsj.com).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit public responses to coverage or viewpoint pieces, send letters to the dedicated letters-to-the-editor channels provided rather than general newsroom addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use corrections/contact addresses for factual errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes contacts for corrections and accuracy inquiries (e.g., New York Times 'Corrections: nytnews@nytimes.com', USA Today 'Corrections: accuracy@usatoday.com').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reporting factual errors or correction requests, use the listed corrections or accuracy-specific addresses to reach the appropriate editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use op-ed and news-tip channels for submitting longer commentary or news tips
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists 'Submit Op-Ed' and 'Write to the news editors: news-tips@nytimes.com' and WSJ 'Submit Op-Ed' / 'Comment on News Articles: newseditors@wsj.com'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send opinion pieces/op-eds or news tips through the channels explicitly labeled for those purposes instead of general feedback addresses to increase the chance of editorial consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social media handles to reach programs and reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Many entries list Twitter handles for programs and anchors (e.g., @CBSEveningNews, @NorahODonnell, @wolfblitzer, @SpecialReport, @BretBaier, @maddow, @LesterHoltNBC, @NYTimes, @Reuters, @AP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, use the listed social handles to address programs/reporters publicly or privately (DMs where supported); the page emphasizes social media as an outreach channel alongside email/forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact radio shows via listed phone numbers, producer emails, or contact forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Radio contacts include NPR contact form and phone (202-513-2000 / 202-513-3232), Sean Hannity Show phone 800-941-7326 (On-Air 3–6 p.m.), and producer contact Lynda McLaughlin: lynda@hannity.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed phone lines during on-air hours for live comment, and use producer emails or station contact forms for submitted comments or program-related messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wire service and news service general contact info for press inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings for wire services include Associated Press info@ap.org and phone, Reuters telephone, United Press International telephone and an editorial contacts list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For broad distribution or to alert wire services to a story or correction, use the general contact emails/phone numbers or department contact lists provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target executive/editorial contacts or departmental lists when available
rubrics_metrics.description: The page mentions 'List of editorial contacts by department' and 'Executive contacts' (e.g., under UPI) and provides general newsroom phone/address info for many outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issue is organizational or requires escalation, use executive or departmental contact lists provided to route messages to the correct editorial decision-makers.
